title.title: The poset determines the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial
title.subtitle: Claim: isomorphic Bruhat intervals, in any Coxeter systems, have equal Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials

plain: Like knowing a building from its floor plan alone: an ordering's shape fixes its special polynomial

beats.text: A Bruhat interval: here all of $S_3$, as an abstract partial order
The polynomials are defined from the group, which the bare poset forgets
The claim: the poset alone fixes the polynomial, across all Coxeter systems

steps: Schedule one interval's edges using the other's reflection order
Bound how much each step can grow: the bounds multiply out
Run it both ways, so each side bounds the other
Every bound is then exact, and the polynomials agree

achievement.label: Combinatorial invariance conjecture (Lusztig and Dyer, 1980s)
achievement.context: Known for lower and short intervals, and length at most 6 (Barkley–Gaetz–Lam, Jan 2026)
achievement.note: The Lean proof cannot follow the paper's route as written

verify.detail: Arbitrary Coxeter systems, polynomials built from scratch. Not in the main-results list
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean statement; we did not build it

voice.text: Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials come from a group. The conjecture: the bare ordering decides them.
Bounds built step by step, run in both directions, are forced to be exact.
Claimed: true for every Coxeter system.
